messages:
Sam: quick thought — gateway currently buffers small requests for 50ms before forwarding to continuous-batcher. thinking we should move to a strict enqueue API and push admission decisions into the batcher. tradeoffs?
Priya: +1 to clear boundary. right now gateway buffering mixes concerns: routing, auth, short-hold. makes observability fuzzy.
Mateo: downside: gateway would need a light-weight enqueue ack path so callers see backpressure quickly. otherwise we get head-of-line latency.
Jin: agree. propose: gateway does a one-way Enqueue RPC that returns 202 + enqueue_id or 503 when batcher rejects. keeps gateway stateless.
Lina: curious about per-tenant fairness — if gateway is stateless, how do we preserve tenant-level quotas? batcher must own credits then.
Sam: exactly — move credit accounting into batcher. gateway forwards tenant_id + hint_tokens. batcher maintains a soft-ledger and returns enrollment/queue position.
Mateo: proto sketch: ```proto
message EnqueueReq { string tenant_id = 1; bytes payload = 2; int32 token_hint = 3; int64 client_ts = 4; }
message EnqueueResp { enum Status { ENQUEUED=0; REJECTED=1; DELAYED=2; } Status status = 1; string enqueue_id = 2; string reason = 3; }
```
Priya: nice. also need a lightweight status endpoint: GET /enqueue/:id to let gateway poll or clients retry.
Jin: for observability we should emit three signals at gateway: forwarded, rejected_by_batcher, enqueue_ack_received. that solves fuzzy metrics.
Lina: what about ordered streams / streaming requests? if gateway only enqueues, streaming attachments must be pinned to the same execution slot. maybe a short-path for tiny streaming (<8 tokens) handled inline by gateway fastpath.
Sam: propose hybrid: gateway fastpath for tiny sync requests (under 8 tokens) that bypasses batcher; everything else goes through Enqueue RPC. keep fastpath opt-in per-route.
Mateo: rollout plan suggestion: 1) implement Enqueue RPC in batcher behind feature flag; 2) gateway starts forwarding and respects 503s; 3) move credit accounting entirely into batcher; 4) enable per-tenant queueing; 5) remove gateway buffering.
Priya: testing matrix: unit tests for enqueue/backpressure, chaos test with surge where batcher responds with DELAYED to validate client retry logic, and perf test with mixed tiny/large workloads.
Jin: concerns: migration period where both systems coexist — need dual-write metrics and a canary region. also think about spike protection: batcher should be able to drop low-priority enqueues early.
Lina: for API semantics, keep human-friendly reason codes (RATE_LIMIT, BUSY, AUTH_FAIL) to avoid opaque 503s.
Mateo: implementation note: use an in-memory soft-ledger + redis fallback for ledger persistence. this keeps latency low and allows cross-process reconciliation.
Sam: ops-bot note: deploy window for refactor should be low-traffic (EU morning). ops-bot: schedule candidate 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC :calendar:
Priya: next steps — I'll draft the RFC addendum with proto + rollout plan. Jin/Mateo can sketch tests. Lina will draft migration observability dashboard.
Jin: cool — I'll PR the EnqueueResp status mapping in the runtime repo.
Lina: +1. also add a dashboard card for enqueue latency percentiles and reject rate by tenant.
Sam: thanks everyone. we'll sync Friday 10am PT to finalize.
__notes: Thread about splitting gateway buffering vs batcher admission; includes proto sketch, rollout plan, metrics and migration notes.
